findings.title: Permissive Wildcard CORS Configuration in Production Setting
findings.description: The FastAPI application initializes CORSMiddleware with allow_origins=['*'] and allow_credentials=True. While settings.ALLOWED_ORIGINS is defined in config.py, it is not passed to the middleware.
findings.impact: Enables any unauthorized third-party origin to make authenticated cross-origin browser requests if credentials or tokens are shared.
findings.remediation: Update CORSMiddleware in backend/app/main.py to use allow_origins=settings.ALLOWED_ORIGINS instead of ['*'].

findings.title: Hardcoded Default Secrets in Configuration Fallback
findings.description: JWT_SECRET_KEY has a static default fallback value ('super-secret-key-habitflow-2026-change-in-production-!'). In production, if an operator does not explicitly define JWT_SECRET_KEY in the environment, tokens could be forged using the known default secret.
findings.impact: Potential token forgery if environment variables are omitted during deployment.
findings.remediation: Enforce mandatory JWT_SECRET_KEY in production environments and add a startup assertion or validator in Settings to reject known insecure default keys.

findings.title: Absence of IP-Based Rate Limiting on Email/Password Login Endpoint
findings.description: While OTP generation and verification endpoints have strict cooldown and 5-attempt limits, the standard /auth/login endpoint does not have rate limiting at the application level.
findings.impact: Vulnerability to automated credential-stuffing or brute-force password guessing attacks without reverse proxy throttling.
findings.remediation: Implement an application-level rate limiter (e.g. slowapi / Redis rate limiter) or reverse proxy rate limiting (e.g. Nginx limit_req) on /api/auth/login.
